newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel deploys tanks in West Bank, around Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israel deploys tanks in West Bank, around Gaza.

text.p: Israel has deployed more tanks and armoured vehicles within striking distance of Palestinian self-rule areas in the West Bank and Gaza despite a drop in violence, Palestinians said on Sunday.
Israel began deploying the armour during clashes and gunbattles in which 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis were killed last week. The clashes began to taper off on Saturday.

On Sunday, Israeli security sources said Israel had activated an operational plan to defend Israelis, the last stage of which includes re-taking areas handed to Palestinian rule under interim peace deals. But they said for now there was no intention of implementing the re-occupation.
Palestinians said the massing of troops did not necessarily mean there was imminent danger of an Israeli invasion. But they said they were watching the Israeli troop movements.
Palestinians in self-rule areas said Israel brought more armour in on Saturday night.
In the West Bank city of Nablus, Palestinians said about 36 tanks and armoured vehicles were dug in behind earth barricades less than one kilometer (half a mile) from the city limits.

Palestinians in Jericho said they saw a total of 26 tanks and armoured personnel carriers around the Jordan Valley enclave. Reinforcements were also reported around other West Bank cities and around the Gaza Strip.

"It's not a secret that we stationed tanks here. We are not bringing them into the Gaza Strip because we think for now there is no need to use them," Israel's Haaretz daily quoted Israeli army southern commander, Major-General Shlomo Yanai, as saying.
"But if the situation necessitates that they be brought in, we will do that without hesitation," Yanai said.

Major General Uzi Dayan, commander of the Israeli army in the West Bank, said in remarks broadcast on Israel Radio on Sunday said that troops were implementing an operation code-named "Field of Thorns" to protect Israelis.

"On Thursday, we activated this plan, stages A and B," Dayan said. "The mission before us is to defend Israelis and vital life lines in our sector, imposition of law and order with strong reaction to any violation and to any risk to Israeli security interests," Dayan said.
Israeli security sources said the plan has a third stage that included the entry of Israeli army forces into the self-rule areas.
Palestinians played down the Israeli movements but said they were watching the situation carefully.
"The massing of troops is a provocative act and is not justified," said Major-General Abdel-Razeq al-Majaydeh, director of the Palestinian security forces in Gaza.
Colonel Saadi Naji, commander of the Palestinian forces in Nablus, said there were contacts with the Israeli side on the troop movements.
"We are following the movement of Israeli vehicles. Things are under control and we are not worried," he told Reuters.
